Subject: DPA execution path — signature order + signatory authority

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the DPA review. We finished an internal pass and have a couple of operational questions before we circulate for signatures:

- Do you prefer DocuSign or AdobeSign for the final execution?
- We need to confirm the routing order (we typically have our procurement and CFO sign before countersign). Is Redwood able to accept a countersign step?
- Please confirm who on Redwood will sign (name + title) and whether you require an authorization letter from our side.

I've attached our latest redlines (Aurelia_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf) and a PDF with our signer authorization. If you can confirm routing and whether we should prepare a single envelope or separate envelopes for the DPA + SOW, that would be helpful.

Best,
Emma
Emma Pritchard
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurelia Health

Attachments: Aurelia_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf, Aurelia_Signer_Authorization.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Pritchard <emma@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA execution path — signature order + signatory authority

Hi Emma — thanks for the files and the clear checklist. Short answers up front:

- Redwood prefers DocuSign for standard contracts (we do AdobeSign for a few partners but the DocuSign flow is faster for multi-signer routing).
- We can accept a countersign step; typical flow is: Aurelia procurement -> Aurelia CFO -> Redwood Legal (countersign). We set Redwood as the final signer by default.
- Authorized Redwood signatory: Rafael Mendes, VP Legal & Compliance. He will countersign on behalf of Redwood.

Rafael — looping you in to confirm you can sign and if you want any envelope settings changed (acknowledgment checkbox, certificate of completion, signer order locked).

Tessa — can you prepare the envelope template and routing order so we can share the DocuSign link back to Aurelia? I've attached a small example routing sheet for your reference.

Emma — if Aurelia needs us to sign first (for their internal procurement reasons), we can make that work but it requires a different envelope configuration (Redwood must be allowed to sign and hand off). Please confirm your preferred signer order.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Signature_Router_Config.xlsx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Emma Pritchard <emma@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA execution path — signature order + signatory authority

Emma / Soojin — quick legal note after reviewing Aurelia's redlines:

1) Subprocessors & transfers: Aurelia's edits to the subprocessor appendix look reasonable; we should add an explicit line referencing SCCs for EU transfers if any EU data processing occurs. If Aurelia can confirm no EU data will be processed for this deployment, we can keep current language.
2) Signature authority: Redwood will countersign via DocuSign. I am authorized to sign for Redwood (VP Legal & Compliance). Please list me as "Rafael Mendes, VP Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference" in the envelope.
3) Envelope settings: please enable caregiver signer order (Procurement -> CFO -> Redwood), require identity verification on the CFO role (ID check), and include the completion certificate.

Operational ask for Aurelia procurement: please attach a scanned signatory authorization that ties the named CFO to their authority (I see the Aurelia_Signer_Authorization.pdf — that should be sufficient).

I'll countersign once the DocuSign envelope is created and you confirm the order.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
VP, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference
